title: structured-output: add CFG + regex constrained-decoding backends and tokenizer edgecase fixes
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Add new constrained decoding backends (CFG grammar engine + regex/FS matcher) for structured output; fix tokenizer edgecases impacting constrained decoding on Unicode/byte-boundary tokens; add tests and docs. Backwards compatible behind feature flag.
description:
Motivation: structured output constraints (CFG/grammar and regex-based constraints) are becoming common in user workloads. Existing constrained-decoding implementation was tightly coupled to a single path and failed on several tokenizer edge cases (Unicode combining marks, multi-byte punctuation, and tokenizers that split regex metacharacters). This PR introduces two new pluggable constrained-decoding backends (a CFG/grammar engine and a lightweight regex/finite-state matcher), improves tokenizer handling, and exposes a feature flag to roll this out gradually.

What I changed: 1) core/backends/constrained_decoding/cfg_engine.py: new CFG-based matcher that compiles user grammars into a compact DP state machine and emits allowed-token masks per step. 2) core/backends/constrained_decoding/regex_fsm.py: regex-backed finite-state matcher optimized for tokenized inputs, with precompiled token-level NFA->DFA steps and failure transitions. 3) core/tokenizer/compat.py: fixes for handling Unicode combining characters, byte-boundary token splits, and escaping meta-characters for regex backends. 4) integration/structured_output/feature_flagging: add structured_output.constrained_decoding.v2 feature flag with rollout and telemetry hooks. 5) tests/structured_output/: ~40 unit/integration tests covering CFG grammars, nested optional groups, greedy vs non-greedy regex constraints, and tokenizer edgecases (emoji, combining marks, ligatures). 6) docs/structured_output.md: usage examples for grammar and regex constraints, migration notes, and performance caveats. 7) perf/benchmarks/constrained_decoding.md: microbenchmarks comparing v1 and v2 backends.

Committed changes are intentionally small per-file but add up across the new backend implementations and tests. The new backends are behind a feature flag and do not change default behavior until the flag is enabled.

Commits (summary): - Add CFG engine for constrained decoding + tests - Add regex-backed FSM matcher + tests - Tokenizer compatibility fixes and escaping utilities - Feature flag and telemetry hooks - Add docs and perf notes - Fix flaky test timing in CI (increase timeout and add deterministic seed)

Files changed (high level): - core/backends/constrained_decoding/cfg_engine.py (new) - core/backends/constrained_decoding/regex_fsm.py (new) - core/backends/constrained_decoding/__init__.py (wiring) - core/tokenizer/compat.py (mod) - integration/structured_output/feature_flagging.py (new) - tests/structured_output/test_cfg_grammar.py (new) - tests/structured_output/test_regex_constraints.py (new) - tests/structured_output/test_tokenizer_edgecases.py (new) - docs/structured_output.md (mod) - perf/benchmarks/constrained_decoding.md (new) - setup for CI/test matrix updates (mod)

CI: Initial runs hit a flaky test (test_tokenizer_edgecases::test_unicode_combining) on Python 3.10 matrix which caused one failed run. I reproduced locally, added a deterministic seed and increased the test timeout; re-ran the CI and all checks passed. Full CI status is now green.

Performance: Microbenchmarks show the CFG engine has ~1.15x token-overhead vs the existing simple constraint path on short grammars, but offers significant expressiveness and reduces application-level post-processing. The regex_fsm backend is comparable to v1 for common regex constraints and faster on token-granular patterns due to precompiled DFA. We added sampling telemetry to monitor production impact.

Compatibility & rollout: The feature is gated by structured_output.constrained_decoding.v2. Default remains the existing implementation. Migration notes in docs include guidance on grammar size, timeout settings, and tokenizer compatibility.

Testing: Added ~40 new unit/integration tests and updated CI matrix to run selected integration tests across tokenizers (byte-level, BPE, sentencepiece). All tests pass in CI.

If merged: enable feature flag gradually and monitor telemetry (constraint_eval.latency, constraint_eval.success_rate).

Related: ENG-9482 (design), ENG-9521 (perf follow-up), SUP-3342 (support ticket reporting tokenizer mismatch).

review_comments: Priya Patel: Great direction — can you add explicit limits to compiled grammar size? Large grammars could blow up memory. Requested: add a config param (max_rules) and validate in the compiler.
Maya Thompson (author): Added max_rules config with default 2000 and unit tests covering the validation. Also added a runtime error with an actionable message linking to docs.

Liam O'Connor: The regex_fsm looks good but please ensure we escape user-supplied strings when building token-level regexes to avoid accidental meta-character interpretation. Also add a benchmark for long regex patterns.
Maya Thompson: Implemented token-escape utilities in core/tokenizer/compat.py and added perf benchmark comparing escaped vs unescaped paths. Benchmarks show negligible overhead.
Jia Chen: Tests are comprehensive. One nit: move the emoji/combining char cases into a dedicated file for readability. Also requested a changelog entry in docs/structured_output.md.
Maya Thompson: Moved tests into test_tokenizer_edgecases.py and added a 'Changelog' subsection in docs with examples and migration tips.

qa_notes: Reproduced tokenization mismatch reported in SUP-3342; fixed by normalizing combining marks before tokenization when feature flag enabled.
